v15: Data Dictionary corrections found by the new controlled-vocabulary invariant in check_links.py. Record_Type gains "EU Legislation", the value carried by all 22 records on the EU Legislation sheet and previously undeclared. General_Type gains "Directive", "Regulation" and "Decision", the EU instrument types in use on that same sheet. No record values were changed - the dictionary was incomplete, not the data. STILL OPEN: Policy_Sector in this workbook declares a ten-term slash-style vocabulary while the records use a mixture of that and the current fourteen-class shared vocabulary; 137 values in this workbook do not match the declaration. The invariant reports these as a warning rather than a failure until the shared vocabulary is reconciled across all three workbooks. See Data/pending_additions.md.

v16: Policy_Sector reconciled, and the Cross-Reference Index put under automatic regeneration. The 14-class shared vocabulary was adopted in indicators workbook v11 (see EXPORT_SCOPING_NOTE section 2.4) and every record sheet in all three workbooks already conformed - a re-check found ZERO non-canonical tokens in any record sheet. The fork was confined to the Cross-Reference Index, a derived sheet that was never regenerated after that migration and is read by nothing, so the drift was invisible until the controlled-vocabulary invariant added in the previous version went looking. This workbook's Data Dictionary now declares the 14 classes in place of the pre-migration slash-style list. The index has been regenerated from its source sheets by the new Data/code/rebuild_xref.py, which finalise.py now runs as step 1 of 4, before the integrity check; hand-editing the index is no longer meaningful and the Data Dictionary says so. The VOCAB_WARN_ONLY debt entry for Policy_Sector has been removed from check_links.py, so Policy_Sector is now a hard gate condition rather than a warning. Details of the rebuild are in the run output and in Data/pending_additions.md.
